title: He wasn’t chasing cattle.
paragraphs:
He wasn’t chasing cattle.
He was chasing control.

And sometimes…
what’s chasing you isn’t love.

You prayed.
You obeyed.
You walked away quietly.

But somehow…
it still found you.

The voice.
The pressure.
The guilt.
The memory of who you used to be.
And now it’s behind you again—loud, accusing, demanding.
What if the thing chasing you only has power because you still feel guilty for leaving it?
Some of us don’t run because we’re afraid.

Ashamed we stayed too long.
Ashamed we tolerated what God never approved.
Ashamed we participated in things we now want freedom from.

Accusing.
Controlling.
Demanding access to a life God already told you to leave.
For years, he lived under Laban’s manipulation.

Wages changed.
Promises broken.
Control disguised as family.

Stayed in it.
Worked through it.
Silently carried it.
“Return to the land of your fathers… and I will be with you.” (Genesis 31:3)
But obedience doesn’t always silence the past immediately.

Genesis 31:23 says:
“Laban took his relatives with him and pursued Jacob for seven days…”
That’s anxiety breathing down your neck.

That’s the fear that maybe…
you didn’t really escape.
And here’s where it cuts deep:

A deceiver.
A manipulator.
A man who once ran from his own consequences.

“Maybe I deserve this.”
“Maybe this is payback.”
“Maybe I’ll never be free.”
Not just what was done to you…
Not when Jacob had everything figured out.
But right in the middle of the chase.

Genesis 31:24
“Then God came to Laban in a dream at night and said to him, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’”
God didn’t just guide Jacob forward.
He restrained what was chasing him.
What chases you does not have the final authority.
And when Laban finally confronts Jacob…

God allows the confrontation not to destroy you—
but to free your voice.
Jacob’s freedom was not rooted in his past being clean.
It was rooted in God’s promise being faithful.
And that points us to something greater.

Sin that we chose.
Moments we knew better.
Patterns we hid.
If your freedom depends on your record being perfect…
This is where Jesus enters the story.
On the cross, Jesus took everything that chases you.

Every accusation.
Every failure.
Every hidden sin.
Every moment of shame.

Colossians 2:14 says:
“He canceled the record of the charges against us and took it away by nailing it to the cross.”
So when the past chases you…
it is chasing a record that no longer exists.

Replaying your failures.
Whispering lies.
Reminding you of who you were.

But Romans 8:1 declares:
“There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”

So why are you still listening to a voice
God has already silenced?
Jacob didn’t win because he outran Laban.
He stood his ground because God stood between them.
And you don’t win by running forever either.
You win by standing in Christ.

Shame says: “You’re still that person.”
Jesus says: “You are made new.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)

Shame says: “Go back.”
God says: “Move forward—I am with you.” (Genesis 31:3)

Shame says: “You owe your past.”
Jesus says: “It is finished.” (John 19:30)
So what are you going to believe?
If you’ve been living under shame…
if you’ve been hearing accusations louder than God’s promises…
if you’ve been afraid that what’s behind you will catch up—
Jesus already stepped into your pursuit.

He took the hit.
He bore the weight.
He silenced the verdict.

Turning from sin.
Turning toward Christ.

“Jesus, I’m done running.
I surrender my past, my shame, my sin.
Forgive me.
Cleanse me.
Lead me forward.
Be my Lord.”

What chases you cannot cancel what God called—
because Jesus already settled your case.
If this stirred something in you…
